title: Frontier source lock
description: The shape of a Frontier's `sources.lock.json`. Every hash in a lock is computed by the resolver from bytes it actually fetched or read; none is ever copied through from the declaration, because a hash nobody computed is worse than no hash at all. This file is the single definition of the shape, and it is what makes the reader invariant below checkable by anything, in any language, without rerunning the resolver.

generated_at.description: When the resolver ran. A lock is a statement about a moment, and a reader that cannot date it cannot tell a stale pin from a current one.

sources.description: Keyed exactly as `sources.yaml` is, so the two join without a mapping table.

commit.description: Read from the GitHub API at generation time, not copied from the declaration. Where the declaration also pins a commit, the resolver fails the run rather than recording a different one.

sha256.description: A content root computed here from the bytes named by `url` or `path`.

exact_roots.description: Per-file content roots computed here, for a repository pinned at a commit whose individual files are the retained evidence. `url` is recorded per file so the root can be recomputed from the same locator the resolver used.

unlocked.description: A sentence saying why no content hash exists for this entry. An entry nobody could pin must never read as one nobody bothered to pin.

error.description: This source should have been lockable and was not. It is written into the lock so the gap is on the record, and the run that wrote it exits non-zero.

oneOf.$comment: The reader invariant: exactly one of sha256, exact_roots, unlocked, error.
